simple.meaning: שְׂכַל (sᵉkal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “consider.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 7:8. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שְׂכַל (H7920) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: שְׂכַל (sᵉkal) / H7920 is traced through Daniel 7:8 with source-language evidence and verse context.

firstOccurrence.englishText: “I considered the horns, and behold, there came up among them another horn, a little one, before which three of the first horns were plucked up by the roots: and behold, in this horn were eyes like the eyes of a man, and a mouth speaking great things.
